suggestion.title: Balance the Shoulders
suggestion.body: Since you have broader shoulders, wearing wide-leg pants or A-line skirts can add beautiful volume to your lower half and create a perfectly balanced silhouette.

suggestion.title: Enhance the V-Taper
suggestion.body: Your build naturally emphasizes the shoulders. A well-fitted polo or a structured jacket will comfortably define your waist without looking too tight, while straight or slightly tapered trousers complete the athletic look.

do: Shirts that flare from the waist
Longline shirts extending below the hips
avoid: Cropped shirts ending at the waist
Simple straight skinny styles without volume

recommended_items.advice: Bootcut jeans gently flare from the knee down, helping balance broader shoulders by adding subtle volume to the lower leg.
Wide-leg jeans create balanced proportions by adding width throughout the lower body, making the silhouette appear more even.
Flared jeans add volume around the lower leg and ankle, helping create a more balanced look for an inverted triangle body shape.
Boyfriend jeans have a relaxed fit that softens the upper body's visual dominance, especially when paired with fitted tops.
Straight-leg jeans create a clean, streamlined silhouette that complements an inverted triangle body shape without emphasizing the shoulders.

avoid_items.advice: Avoid skinny jeans, as they can emphasize the contrast between broader shoulders and narrower hips, making the upper body appear wider.

general_advice: Choose mid-rise or high-rise jeans to help define the waist and create a more balanced overall silhouette.

recommended_items.advice: Tulip skirts add soft volume around the hips, helping create a more balanced silhouette for an inverted triangle body shape.
Box pleated skirts create structure and fullness in the lower body, balancing broader shoulders.
A-line skirts gently flare from the waist, creating the illusion of wider hips and a more proportional figure.
Bias-cut skirts skim the body gracefully while adding subtle movement that enhances balance.
Layered skirts add visual volume to the lower body, helping offset a broader upper body.
Ruffled skirts introduce texture and fullness around the hips, creating a more balanced appearance.
Paneled skirts add shape and structure to the lower body, improving overall proportions.
Straight skirts create a clean silhouette while maintaining balance when paired with the right top.
Circle skirts add generous volume and movement, making the lower body appear fuller and more proportional.
Full skirts create volume around the hips and legs, balancing a broader shoulder line.
Ballerina skirts add softness and fullness, drawing attention to the lower half of the body.
Tiered skirts create layers and volume that enhance the appearance of the hips and lower body.

general_advice: Skirts with extra volume or dropped waistlines help create the illusion of fuller hips and a more balanced silhouette.

recommended_items.advice: Wrap dresses define the waist and create balanced proportions by drawing attention to the body's center.
Sheath dresses create a sleek silhouette while highlighting the waist for a balanced look.
A-line dresses gently flare from the waist, creating the illusion of fuller hips.
One-shoulder dresses break the symmetry of broad shoulders, creating a softer and more balanced appearance.
Apron dresses add structure while drawing attention toward the waist and lower body.
Peplum dresses add volume around the hips, helping balance broader shoulders.
Fit-and-flare dresses emphasize the waist and create fullness in the skirt for a flattering silhouette.
Shift dresses provide a relaxed silhouette that doesn't overemphasize the upper body.
Paneled dresses use strategic seams to create shape and improve body proportions.
Dresses with a nipped waist highlight the waistline and create the appearance of balanced curves.
